SAR-Plan

Air Search Methodology Route Engine
Class Demo
Prioritized search areas for a missing-aircraft flight plan. Strategy layer only: where to look, in what order.
Method & lineage

New Two-Area Method (NTAM) as revised by Desmarais (2000). NTAM developed by the Canadian DND Directorate of Air Operational Research (DAOR) from 76 missing-aircraft missions, Canada 1981–1986. Validated for CONUS by Desmarais on 78 AFRCC missions from 1999 (62 actual). NTAM performed worse in the US than Canada (Area One 65% vs 79%; Area Two 69% vs 83% on actual missions); Desmarais' revised second area reached ~82% of actual missing aircraft, which is the default here.

Source: Civil Air Patrol — Missing Aircraft Search Research (June 2009), Sec. 3, J. W. Desmarais, CAP, 2000.

Flight plan

LKP · last known position
Turning points / waypoints
Ordered LKP → DEST. Turning points shape the search corridor; Area 2 circles are drawn at LKP and destination only.
DEST · destination
Type a US airport identifier (ICAO KAPA, IATA ASE, or FAA LID 0CO0) and pick from the list, or enter coordinates as lat, lon (decimal or DMS/DDM with N/S/E/W). LKP updates first-class: retype it as leads come in.
Method parameters (defaults pre-filled)
Area 2 radius is computed: R = max(min radius, fraction × total track length).

Search map

Scroll/pinch to zoom · drag to pan · click for coordinates · switch basemaps top-right (online layers need internet) · Measure for distances.

Prosecution sequence

Search areas per the New Two-Area Method (DAOR, Canada, 1981–86) as revised by J. Desmarais (CAP, 2000), validated on 78 AFRCC missions. NTAM-Desmarais-2000.
